subject: Observability ask: per-customer route breakdown & anomalous tail-latency explorer
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Tom Caldwell <tc@brightbank.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Observability ask: per-customer route breakdown & anomalous tail-latency explorer

Hi all,

Brightbank has flagged two blocker items for our pilot: (1) they need a per-customer/per-route cost waterfall so their finance and engineering teams can map token spend back to their internal product routes, and (2) they want an "anomalous tail-latency explorer" so they can quickly pivot to traces and request IDs when they see 95th/99th percentile spikes.

They shared a small sample of token logs (attached) and a quick sketch of what they'd like in the Console (attached). They asked for an estimate and a rough timeline so they can decide whether to expand the pilot in August.

High-level asks:
- Per-route cost breakdown (tokens, model variant, quantization profile) with time-range and smoothing options
- Ability to group routes by tag or customer-provided route metadata
- A drilldown workflow from an observed latency spike to the underlying request IDs and KV cache hits/misses
- Exportable CSV and a simple API endpoint for programmatic pulls (Brightbank wants to feed this into their internal billing)

Can the Observability and Serving teams weigh in on feasibility, instrumentation gaps, and rough engineering estimates? Priyom — FYI on the commercial timing. Laura — any procurement/contract implications if we ship a bespoke export endpoint for them?

Thanks,
Camila

--
Camila Reyes
Account Lead, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: brightbank_sample_token_logs.csv (csv), per-route-ui-mock.png (image)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability ask: per-customer route breakdown & anomalous tail-latency explorer

Thanks for the context, Camila. Quick notes from infra/serving side:

- We can surface per-route token accounting if routes are consistently tagged on the request. Currently we ingest route as free-form metadata; aggregations exist but are not exposed in the Console as a cost waterfall.
- The CSV looks fine for sampling; we'll need to standardize a minimal schema (request_id, timestamp, route, model, tokens_in/tokens_out, kv_cache_hit) — I can draft that.
- Tail-latency explorer: we have the necessary telemetry (latency histograms, traces with request_id) but we don't have a UI flow that ties 95/99 pctl anomalies to a trace/trace-id link. Building a lightweight drilldown is feasible as a Console feature — depends on how deep the trace popover needs to be.

Blockers / questions:
1) Route metadata hygiene: can Brightbank promise stable route names or route tags? If not, we need to add a mapping layer in the Console.
2) Export API: are we building a one-off endpoint for Brightbank or a generic API? Generic will take longer but has product value.

Estimate (ballpark):
- MVP per-route waterfall UI + standardized export CSV: ~3 engineers x 4 weeks (backfill testing/QA)
- Tail-latency explorer (drill to trace + request metadata): ~2 engineers x 3 weeks if we reuse current trace store links

I opened a ticket INF-4721 and added a short tech spec. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4721

I'll sync with David to confirm trace integration details.

Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 12:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability ask: per-customer route breakdown & anomalous tail-latency explorer

Adding details from Observability side:

- Current telemetry: we emit per-request metrics with request_id, model_name, route_name (if provided), latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, and kv_cache_hit boolean. The Prometheus/TSDB captures histograms but we only surface aggregated dashboards at service level today.
- Work required:
  * Ingest: minor schema normalization (log forwarder change) — ~2 days of infra work to ensure route tags are normalized, add route_id mapping.
  * Query layer: create rollup that computes token cost by model per route — depends on pricing config (we'll reuse existing pricing table). ~5 days dev.
  * UI: waterfall visualization + threshold alerting UI — depends on Console frontend bandwidth, estimate 3 weeks.

Operational considerations:
- We should add a per-customer sampling policy for traces to avoid increased tracing cost. Brightbank may want full traces for spikes; propose a rule that captures full traces only when latency > 95th percentile + a backend-specified rate limit.
- For exports, we can provide a signed S3 presigned URL where nightly CSVs are dropped; simpler than a new API. If Brightbank insists on API, that moves scope.

I've attached a quick mock of the desired Console panel (per-route-ui-mock.png) and a sanitized token-log snapshot (brightbank_sample_token_logs.csv).

-David

Thanks team — this looks reasonable. Two commercial notes:

- Brightbank made it clear that this visibility is a gating factor for the pilot expansion. If we can commit to an MVP in ~4–6 weeks, they will sign an expansion term that looks like a $120k ARR add-on (deal_id BBK-2026-EXPAND).
- If we go with the S3 nightly export approach, finance/legal will want a short addendum allowing automated delivery for their billing system. Laura, can you advise what that addendum should look like and whether we need a formal procurement PO?

Camila — please capture acceptance criteria and I'll put a conditional milestone into the commercial plan. Rishi/David — if the INF-4721 scope changes materially vs the estimates, flag immediately so we can re-negotiate timing.

Priyom
